norms.text: A stranger is housed under the elder's roof and fed from the guest stores.
Quarrels and debts between households go to the elder.
Offerings at the foot of the tree are kept filled.

taboos.text: Taking from the offering bowls at the tree's foot.
Lifting a hatchery lid without a keeper.

values.text: A kin-house swept for whoever comes back from downriver.

contempts.text: Gang bosses who keep a hand on the roll past the season.

place.text: Too big now for the people left in it; the tree is why anyone stays.

work.text: The roll is the only coin; whether it is worth the strain on the tree divides the village.

danger.text: River predators on the approach; jellies in the shallows; a moon adder under the bank.

rumour.text: Talk is of the tree going quiet.

directions.text: Ways are given by the river: a day down to the gang camp, the port past it.

addressTerms.text: A stranger is called by what they are doing or what they want; neighbours by name.

neverSaid.text: How long a neighbour's kin have been gone, said to that neighbour.

grievances.text: More adults go downriver on the roll every year and fewer come back up.

rumours.text: The tree has begun to go quiet.

views.text: The port and the gangs take the village's people and send back coin.

dissent.text: The tree marks every adult on the roll and shows the strain; she reads that strain.
The gang families downriver were hatched under this Hist and still claim it; she sells to their camp and resents every word of the claim.
